claims.text: High-entropy nanoalloys contain multiple principal elements in near-equal proportions.
Adding a small amount of tungsten can improve the structural stability of high-entropy nanoalloys at high temperatures.
Adding a small amount of tungsten can improve the chemical stability of high-entropy nanoalloys at high temperatures.
The proposed tungsten addition is 1–5 at.%.
The tungsten-induced stability improvement should hold above 800 °C.
Tungsten addition will form a stable, dispersed phase of tungsten-rich nanoparticles.
Alternatively, tungsten addition will form a stable tungsten-containing solid solution.
Tungsten has a high melting point and high thermal stability because it is a refractory metal.
A stable tungsten-containing phase will hinder grain growth.
A stable tungsten-containing phase will reduce diffusion rates.
A stable tungsten-containing phase will decrease the formation of detrimental phases.
Relative to an otherwise identically processed alloy without tungsten, tungsten addition will improve resistance to microstructural degradation.
Relative to an otherwise identically processed alloy without tungsten, tungsten addition will improve oxidation resistance.
Relative to an otherwise identically processed alloy without tungsten, tungsten addition will improve corrosion resistance.
The resulting stability improvements will enhance high-temperature performance and lifespan.
The stability improvement will remain significant up to approximately 1000 °C.
Above approximately 1000 °C, other degradation mechanisms may dominate.
The optimal tungsten concentration and operative mechanisms may depend on alloy composition and processing conditions.
Tungsten addition may alter strength or ductility, but the nature of those changes is not established.
